extracted.intended_audience: students and educated readers of natural philosophy / physics / biology
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition of the principles and modes of 'equilibration' in physical, astronomical, geological, and biological systems, illustrated by examples (tops, steam-engines, the Solar System, organisms). Aims to state general laws and orders of equilibration and their consequences for evolution and distribution of matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate equilibration of component motions
rubrics_metrics.description: The various motions which an aggregate possesses are separately equilibrated: those which are smallest, or which meet with the greatest resistance, or both, disappearing first; and leaving at last, that which is greatest, or meets with least resistance, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by the spinning top example and other instances (ship's bell, stream surface, arrested bullet): subordinate motions (horizontal momentum, 'wabbling') are dissipated first by air resistance and surface irregularities or gyroscopic opposition, leaving the chief rotatory motion to continue until friction/atmosphere dissipate it. Emphasizes that equilibration often removes some movements while others continue unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equilibrium mobile arises when internal relative motions meet little external resistance
rubrics_metrics.description: When the aggregate has a movement of its parts with respect to each other, which encounters but little external resistance, there is apt to be established an equilibrium mobile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a spinning top whose relative internal motions are little resisted may exhibit a moving equilibrium (equilibrium mobile) where the top appears stationary despite internal rotation. More generally applies to systems where relative motions persist but the centre of gravity of the whole is stationary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moving equilibrium tends to lapse into complete equilibrium
rubrics_metrics.description: This moving equilibrium eventually lapses into complete equilibrium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noted as a general tendency over time as dissipative processes (resistance, radiation) slowly reduce relative motions; e.g., planetary motions may be very slowly diminished by ethereal resistance leading ultimately (inconceivably remote) to complete equilibrium.

rubrics_metrics.name: First order of equilibration: simple/projectile motions dissipated
rubrics_metrics.description: The first order includes the comparatively simple motions, as those of projectiles, which are not prolonged enough to exhibit their rhythmical character; but which, being quickly divided and subdivided into motions communicated to other portions of matter, are presently dissipated in the rhythm of ethereal undulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are short-lived sensible motions that are rapidly transferred and lost into finer-scale (molecular/ethereal) motions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second order of equilibration: vibrations and oscillations (visible rhythm)
rubrics_metrics.description: The second order, comprehending the various kinds of vibration or oscillation as usually witnessed, the motion is used up in generating a tension which, having become equal to it or momentarily equilibrated with it, thereupon produces a motion in the opposite direction, that is subsequently equilibrated in like manner: thus causing a visible rhythm, that is, however, soon lost in invisible rhythms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ordinary oscillatory phenomena where visible rhythms decay into imperceptible (molecular/ethereal) motions; explanation of how tension generation and reversal produce damped rhythms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third order: dependent moving equilibrium (continuous input equals expenditure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The third order of equilibration obtains in those aggregates which continually receive as much motion as they expend — e.g., the steam engine (especially that which feeds its own furnace and boiler) supplies an example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Called 'dependent moving equilibrium': the dissipated force is from moment to moment replaced by external supply; balance maintained by raising or lowering expenditure according to supply variation (each increase/decrease of steam results in rise/fall of engine movement bringing it to balance with changed resistance). This order is commonly met throughout phases of Evolution and in terrestrial/organic cycles (circulation of water, meteorological processes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fourth order: independent/perfect moving equilibrium (Solar System)
rubrics_metrics.description: The equilibration to be distinguished as of the fourth order is the independent or perfect moving equilibrium — illustrated in the rhythmical motions of the Solar System; which, being resisted only by a medium of inappreciable density, undergo no sensible diminution in such periods of time as we can measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System-level moving equilibrium where relative motions are continually counter-balanced so the mean state of the whole remains practically constant; constituents retain relative motion while centre of gravity of group is fixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: All equilibrations are relative, not absolute (centre of gravity loses motion)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the highest point of view, all these kinds of equilibration may be regarded as different modes of one kind: the balance arrived at is relative, and not absolute — a cessation of the motion of some particular body in relation to a certain point or points, involving neither the disappearance of the relative motion lost (simply transformed into other motions), nor a diminution of the body's motions with respect to other points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generalization: in every aggregate it is the centre of gravity only that loses its motion; constituents retain relative motions (molecules if none else). Thus every equilibrium commonly regarded as absolute is in one sense a moving equilibrium, and vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moving equilibrium as penultimate state in evolution and structural redistribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout Evolution of all kinds, there is a continual approximation to, and more or less complete maintenance of, this moving equilibrium. The evolution of every aggregate must go on until this equilibrium mobile is established; since an excess of force which the aggregate possesses in any direction must eventually be expended in overcoming resistances to change in that direction — leaving behind only those movements which compensate each other and form a moving equilibrium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequent structural state: arrangement of forces counterbalancing all forces to which aggregate is subject. As long as residual force exists in any direction, redistribution of matter must continue. The limit of heterogeneity toward which every aggregate progresses is formation of specializations and combinations of parts matching specialized combined forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nebular/planetary examples: transitional moving equilibria (spheroid, rings, planet formation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those successively changed forms arising during the evolution of the Solar System (if nebular hypothesis is granted) were transitional kinds of moving equilibrium, each giving place to more permanent kinds on the way towards complete equilibration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: assumption of oblate spheroidal figure by condensing nebulous matter is a temporary moving equilibrium; genesis of nebulous rings implies perfect balancing of aggregative and centrifugal forces — ring progresses toward more complete moving equilibrium, dissipation of motions leads to concentration into planetary bodies with residuary relative motions nearly perfectly equilibrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solar and cosmic equilibration: dissipation of sensible motion into molecular motion; sun's heat reserve being expended
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion of masses produced during Evolution is being slowly re-diffused into molecular motion of the ethereal medium through progressive integration of each mass and resistance to motion through space. The force known to us in solar radiations is the changed form of some other force of which the Sun is the seat; by gradual dissipation of these radiations into space this other force is being slowly exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses Helmholtz's estimates and the notion that the Sun's heat/ light are being expended and will in remote future diminish, illustrating equilibration by transformation of sensible motion to insensible molecular motion. Emphasizes uncertainty in numerical estimates but general proposition of exhaustion of the Sun's reserve stands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earth's figure and rotation: equilibrium of gravity and centrifugal force; tidal friction effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A spherical figure alone can equilibrate forces of mutually-gravitating atoms; if aggregate has rotatory motion the form of equilibrium becomes a spheroid of oblateness according to rotation rate. The Earth is an oblate spheroid diverging from sphericity to counterbalance centrifugal force from axial rotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only remaining process for Earth as a whole is loss of axial motion; tidal friction is a real cause of decreasing rotation (extremely slow), exemplifying universal progress toward equilibrium. Notes that ultimate extremes would be reached only in infinite or inconceivably remote time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terrestrial processes as dependent moving equilibria (winds, waves, circulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Winds, waves, streams, and the denudations and depositions they effect perpetually illustrate the gradual dissipation of motions and tendency towards a balanced distribution of forces. These complex movements of aerial, liquid, and solid matter on Earth's crust constitute a dependent moving equilibrium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: unceasing circulation of water between ocean and land as compensating actions maintaining an average; as solar input decreases, sensible motions produced by it must decrease and re-distributions of matter on Earth's surface will diminish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biological/homeostatic equilibration: four-fold manifestation and vis medicatrix naturae
rubrics_metrics.description: Every living body exhibits the process in four-fold form — in balancing mechanical forces moment-to-moment; balancing functions hour-to-hour; changes of state year-to-year; and finally in the complete arrest of vital movements at death. Organic functions constitute a dependent moving equilibrium fed by intake (food) replacing dissipated motive power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: limits of systole/diastole show momentary equilibrium; increased exertion leads to increased respiration and circulation to regenerate force; deviations are restored or equilibrated about a new mean if changed permanently. Disturbances not overturning life are eventually corrected (vis medicatrix naturae); even persistent derangement leads to a new equilibrated normal.
